$comment: THE ONE PLACE that says where every shipped throwable cue came from and under what licence. Edit this, then run `node scripts/audio/build-throwable-cues.mjs --sources <dir>` (needs ffmpeg). It writes public/sounds/throwables/<cue>.webm + .m4a, public/sounds/throwables/CREDITS.md and src/throwables/cueManifest.generated.ts. A `placeholder` cue has no file yet and names the legacy ThrowableSoundService recipe to play in its place; tests/unit/throwableCuesAreLicensed.test.ts counts them and refuses any licence not in `allowedLicenses`. Plan: docs/throwables/THROWABLES-PREMIUM-ANIMATION-PLAN.md 3.3.1.

own-synthesis.title: Smarter.Poker - synthesised cues
own-synthesis.author: Smarter.Poker
own-synthesis.recipe: ffmpeg lavfi sources (aevalsrc / anoisesrc) shaped by the per-layer `filter` in this manifest, then loudness-normalised with every other cue. The expression IS the provenance: nothing is downloaded, nobody is credited, and the file is reproducible from this repo alone. Used only where no CC0 sample pack has the sound - a rising firework whistle, a low rumble and a champagne fizz bed are not in Kenney's libraries, and Freesound needs an API key nobody has supplied yet (plan 3.3.1, phase 6).

pop_soft.$comment: beer: mug 2 pops in (reference: a soft pop, centroid ~1.9 kHz).

glass_clink_rattle.$comment: beer + champagne: the reference chime has six rattles at 0 / 133 / 380 / 466 / 600 / 733 ms and a 1.3 s ring-down. Built from five glass impacts layered at those offsets with decaying gain, plus the interface 'glass' tone underneath for the ring.

drip_tick.$comment: cracked_egg: the faint tick as the white drips.

squirt_start.$comment: water_gun: the first squirt. Needs a Freesound CC0 water-pistol take (phase 6).

squirt_loop.$comment: water_gun: 2.5 s pump + hiss loop. Needs a Freesound CC0 take (phase 6).

splat_wet.$comment: tomato + poop: one wet splat 33 ms after the visual burst. Needs a Freesound CC0 take (phase 6).

egg_crack.$comment: cracked_egg: the crack. Needs a Freesound CC0 take (phase 6).

cork_pop.$comment: champagne 800: the loudest cue in the library. A wood impact for the thock plus an interface drop for the airy 'pop' tail; the reference's cork is a short resonant burst with almost no ring.

fizz_loop.$comment: champagne 1000-3200: the foam bed under the jet. Band-limited white noise, which is what a fizz is; no sample pack here has one and the expression is reproducible.

flute_clink.$comment: champagne 3167: two flutes meeting. Brighter and shorter than the beer mugs' six-rattle chime - a flute rings once and cleanly.

flute_clink_soft.$comment: champagne 3900 / 4100: the two late soft clinks the capture records with the table hidden.

fw_whistle.$comment: fireworks 0-830: the rising whistle, measured centroid 5.3-5.6 kHz, swelling from the first spark and peaking as burst 1 opens. A quadratic chirp 900 Hz -> ~5.4 kHz with a breath of air noise under it. Synthesised: no CC0 pack here has a firework whistle.

fw_crackle.$comment: fireworks: the bang cluster around bursts 2 and 3 - the reference lands one bang every 130-170 ms. Six plate and metal impacts at exactly those spacings, decaying.

fw_rumble.$comment: fireworks 1767-2033: the tail that bridges the gap and wave 2's trails, 25-60x the median with NO picture on screen. Brown noise under 220 Hz. Synthesised for the same reason as the whistle.

fw_barrage.$comment: fireworks 2333: wave 2, the loudest hit of the throw (RMS 0.406, second loudest in the whole video). Eight impacts, densest at the front, with the rumble layered under the opening.

harp_sparkle.$comment: rose 767: one soft sparkle running 1.6 s under the butterfly. Six plucks up a pentatonic run, decaying - the reference's cue is a rising shimmer, not a chord.
